title: From 20 Years Ago: Eagle Bill, The Loss of A Good Man and Vaporizer Pioneer. Bill's Life Will Long Be Recognized As A Rebuke to Medical Establishment For Its Failure to Recognize the Vaporization of Cannabis.

content_html_sanitized:
As I like to say about marijuana prohibition generally, we couldn’t make this up. I came across this obituary in the MarijuanaNews archives today and it brought back some memories.

First and foremost, no writer of fiction could or would have conjured up someone as improbable as “Eagle Bill”.

 

I had known him for several years, but I had no idea what his real name was, just “Eagle Bill”, which was based on his Native American ancestry.

 

I saw him every year when I was in Amsterdam for the Cannabis Cup, and he was set up at the Dronkers’ Sensi Hemp Museum, demonstrating vaporization with a big bell jar and a heat gun to a group that was otherwise very experienced with cannabis.

 

I remember Bill telling me that he had been invited to Germany to demonstrate it to a group of German doctors, who were decades ahead of the current German medical establishment.

From 1998,

See German Drug Czar Calls For Medical Marijuana: "The suffering of patients with illnesses such as MS, Cancer or AIDS could be eased with cannabis."

And

German Association for Cannabis as Medicine Gives International Coverage To The Issues

But from 2025

The New German Health Minister, A Lawyer, Not A Doctor, Wants To Make It Harder For Elderly Germans to Get Medical Cannabis. Of Course She Wouldn’t Put It That Way

 

As I said twenty years ago, “I wanted this good man to get the recognition that he deserved, but also I never wanted it to be forgotten that organized quackery with its arrogant credentialism lagged far behind this kindly and humble soul.”

 

We have come a long way since then, but we obviously still have a long way to go. RIP Eagle Bill🙏

See

Remarkable Press Release: “The DEA's BILLION Dollar Marijuana Scandal: A DEA Regulatory Betrayal of Science and Public Trust”

 

Originally Posted July 6, 2005 edited
Analysis by Richard Cowan

It is with much sadness that I belatedly note the passing of my old friend Eagle Bill, a really good man and by an odd twist of fate, the vaporizer pioneer. He died in his sleep on May 22nd.

 

When I saw him at last year's Cannabis Cup in Amsterdam, Bill was clearly in bad health, but he was as cheerful as always. Bill was well-practiced at putting on a brave face. He suffered chronic pain for many years as the result of an accident that had left him with a bad limp. Consequently, he was a medical user of cannabis himself and understood the importance of alternatives to smoking for some patients.

Bill had already become a lay expert on vaporizing cannabis, when I first got to know him in 1996. Despite having no scientific education, he was sometimes called upon to demonstrate the technique to European doctors, but not in his native US.
See
No Medicine Is Smoked. Okay, But Why Isn't Cannabis Sold Over-the-Counter? New MAPS/NORML Vaporizer Study Undermines Key Part Of Prohibitionist Party Line On Smoked-Marijuana.

It is ironic that he passed away just as vaporization was finally getting some official recognition.

Over the years, whenever the topic of vaporization came up, I always made a point of citing Bill's pioneering work. I did this for two reasons. I wanted this good man to get the recognition that he deserved, but also I never wanted it to be forgotten that organized quackery with its arrogant credentialism lagged far behind this kindly and humble soul.

 

I would also like to take this opportunity to salute Alan and Ben Dronkers of Sensi Seeds for giving Bill a place at their Hemp Museum where he could demonstrate vaporization to visitors.
